newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban state sugar firm names acting head - sources.
newsitem.headline: Cuban state sugar firm names acting head - sources.

text.p: Cuba's state sugar trading firm Cubazucar has removed its longstanding president, Alberto Betancourt, and has a temporary new head, industry sources said Monday.
William Parra, a former deputy president of the organisation, is currently acting president, the sources said.
Parra was not immediately available for comment Monday.

No reason has emerged yet for the replacement late in December of Betancourt, who had headed Cubazucar for years and was a familiar and well-respected figure on international sugar markets. There was also no word on whether he has been given another job.
Officials from the Sugar Ministry, consulted about the case, referred calls to the Foreign Trade Ministry. No official from that ministry was available immediately to comment.
In the past two years Betancourt had been in part responsible for securing foreign financing for technnical input in the sugar harvests.

This financing, which began in 1995 to the tune of more than $120 million, helped Cuba halt a disastrous slide in its cane production. The harvest in 1995-96 was 4.45 million tonnes, a sharp increase on the previous year's dismal 3.3 million tonnes.
On financing for this year's crop, Sugar Minister Nelson Torres said last month that the island had secured foreign credits for all 13 of the sugar producing provinces.
Torres said in reply to a question that the total sum involved in financing was slightly more than $320 million, including the province-by-province funding, but did not break down the figure.
Officials have no given a target for the harvest but they are expecting a more modest improvement. Some experts have said the figure will probably be about 4.8 million tonnes.

There has been no mention of Bentacourt's removal in Cuba's state-run media. But it is not uncommon in Cuba for replacements or sackings of key figures in the state sector to take place with no announcement in the media.
